An independent mandatory manager guard refuses forbidden module-service execution before the first executor spawn. Cover canonical identities/aliases/cached and direct/coalesced activation; unknown universe or ownership refuses the candidate.

Independent executor guard checks before every final-target exec path, including generic fallback. This is defense in depth: if executor spawn occurred, preserve consumption/uncertainty and stop; do not call it a zero-exec barrier.
No six-role expansion, module permit, broker loan/refund, replacement deadline or restart. Existing provisional allocations stay unchanged.

Global module-service denial scope is restricted to the qualified dedicated host; selective FC1 attribution is insufficient under merged/shared jobs. Preexisting work/policy epoch or unknown aliases makes admission fail.
Guard and denial-receipt overhead must fit the original CPU/time/memory/storage/I/O lifecycle caps with no new process/helper/service activation. Unknown cost remains a stop, not zero-cost evidence.

Source guard, synthetic trace or absence of observed exec is not a qualified pre-effect witness; independent source/object/host and future separately authorized native-negative checks remain required.
